researcher_notes: CALIBRATION RUN. Single file '747505-040.pdf' ('BT reflex Autopilot' reach truck line, brand note: the document's own footer states 'TOYOTA MATERIAL HANDLING IN EUROPE, MANAGING THE TOYOTA AND BT MATERIALS HANDLING BRANDS IN EUROPE' -- BT is a Toyota-owned brand, same company) is a genuine VARIANT-COMPLETION case: it documents 3 payload variants sharing one physical chassis family (RAE160=1600kg, RAE200=2000kg, RAE250=2500kg). RAE160 and RAE250 already exist in the DB; RAE200 does NOT exist and is added as a new product. NAMING INCONSISTENCY FLAG: the existing DB entry for RAE160 is named 'Toyota RAE160 Autopilot' (no 'Reflex') while the existing RAE250 entry is named 'Toyota Reflex RAE250 Autopilot' (with 'Reflex') even though both come from the exact same product line/brand ('BT reflex'). I named the new RAE200 entry 'Toyota RAE200 Autopilot' to match its closer sibling RAE160's existing convention, but flag this pre-existing DB naming inconsistency (RAE160 vs RAE250) for a human to reconcile -- ideally all three should use the same naming pattern. METHODOLOGY NOTE on min_aisle_width (KO field, high-stakes): this datasheet's aisle-width table (p.4) is a matrix of Model x Mast type x Battery compartment (mm) x Rotation mode ('Rotate on point' vs 'Rotate with radius 400mm') x Load dimensions (800x1200 / 1000x1200 / 1200x800 / 1200x1000mm), i.e. NOT a single number per model. I used the smallest 'Rotate on point' value at the smallest available battery compartment for each model (the industry-standard Ast/right-angle-stack convention, consistent with the Jungheinrich EKS 215a spec sheet's own 'Arbeitsgangbreite' convention processed in the same session) -- RAE160=2694mm (275mm battery compartment, load 800x1200), RAE200=2801mm (347mm compartment), RAE250=2886mm (419mm compartment, smallest available for that model). This is a reasonable, defensible reading but the true minimum achievable aisle for a specific buyer configuration could differ; flag for review before treating as a hard KO cutoff. CONFLICT FOUND: existing DB value for RAE250's min_aisle_width (3071mm) does not match ANY cell in this datasheet's aisle-width table for RAE250 (closest values range 2876-3336mm across all documented configs, but 3071 itself does not appear) -- likely sourced from a different config or a different document originally; flagged, not overwritten. SECOND CONFLICT: existing DB value for RAE160's lifting_height is 11000mm, but this datasheet's own footnote (p.3, 'Max lift height 9500mm' for the 347/419/491mm battery compartments; 7500mm for the base 275mm compartment) never states a lift height above 9500mm for RAE160 -- even though the printed Mast Dimensions table (p.3) has a column going up to 10000mm, which is itself inconsistent with the document's own footnote and may be a documentation artifact in Toyota's own PDF. Neither reading reaches 11000mm. Flagged as a conflict, not overwritten -- the existing DB value may originate from a different/newer Toyota datasheet not in this batch. max_gradient convention: used the WITH-LOAD figure (loaded vehicle climbing capability), consistent with the AP0 field hint ('the loaded unit') and with the existing RAE250 DB value (7.0, which matches the with-load column '7/12' exactly, confirming this is the correct convention to use for RAE160/RAE200 too).
